rule.description: Always load and follow ./.ai-rules.xml before any code generation step.

allowedTechnologies.database: MySQL via ORM (no raw driver usage)

subrule.description: Create modern, clean, and professional UI design using Tailwind CSS with a clear visual hierarchy
Establish strong typography hierarchy: use heading levels (h1-h6) consistently with appropriate font sizes, weights, and spacing to create clear information structure
Maintain consistent spacing using Tailwind's spacing scale throughout all components and layouts
Ensure accessible color contrast ratios (WCAG AA compliant) for all text and interactive elements
Use semantic HTML5 elements to reinforce content structure and improve accessibility
Implement responsive design that works seamlessly across all device sizes (mobile, tablet, desktop)
Only override styles via Tailwind's @apply or custom CSS when absolutely necessary to maintain consistency
Avoid using Emojis in professional interface elements
Include high-quality, optimized images where applicable to enhance visual appeal without compromising performance

rule.description: Each page or feature must be implemented as its own FastAPI router (using APIRouter) with its own templates and static sub-folder.

Place the JQuery code for each page in a separate JavaScript file named after the blueprint and located at static/js/<blueprint-name>.js. Include it only in the corresponding template via {% block page_js %}.

Create reusable Jinja2 components (macros) for common UI elements such as navbar, sidebar, footer, flash messages, and buttons. Store them in templates/components/ and import with {% from 'components/navbar.html' import navbar %}. Pass context explicitly to each macro.

Use MySQL exclusively through an ORM (no direct driver calls); implement a session/connection management layer in db_utils.py that provides a per-request ORM session via FastAPI dependencies or middleware, relying on the ORM/driver for efficient connection pooling.
Auto-reload the FastAPI dev server on code/template/static changes by running Uvicorn with the --reload flag; configure the Jinja2 environment (if used) with auto_reload = True in development only.
Ship a lightweight health-check endpoint /health that returns { "status": "ok", "timestamp": "" } and performs a minimal ORM-based query (e.g., SELECT 1) against the pooled MySQL database.

Store all sensitive secrets (APP_SECRET_KEY, DATABASE_URL, etc.) in a config.json file located in the project root; load it at startup with json.load(). Never commit config.json to git; provide a sample config.example.json instead.

The root route ('/') must serve index.html as the main entry point of the application. This should be implemented in the main app or a dedicated blueprint to ensure visitors land on the intended homepage.

Use the ORM's migration tooling (e.g., Alembic for SQLAlchemy) to manage the MySQL schema via Python migration scripts in a migrations/ folder. Each migration file should be numbered (001_initial.py, 002_add_users.py) and include both upgrade and downgrade routines.
Code Quality and Function Design: Write clean, functional, and easy-to-understand code without OOP

subrule.description: Use pure functions where possible - functions should have clear inputs and outputs without side effects
Keep functions small and focused on a single responsibility (max 20-30 lines per function)
Use descriptive function names that clearly indicate their purpose (verb-noun format)
Include docstrings for all functions explaining purpose, parameters, return values, and any side effects
Avoid deep nesting - use early returns and guard clauses to flatten code structure
Use meaningful variable names that describe their purpose, avoiding single-letter names except for simple iterators
Follow PEP 8 style guidelines for consistent formatting and naming conventions
Use type hints for function parameters and return values to improve readability
Structure code with clear separation of concerns - database logic, business logic, and presentation logic should be separated
Avoid global variables - use function parameters and return values to pass data between functions

rule.description: Comment Formatting: All comments must be written only as multi-line ASCII box blocks with a top and bottom border of dashes and vertical bar-prefixed lines inside.

rule.description: Application Entry and Environment Management: Do not create virtual environments or separate runner scripts; the application must be started directly from a single app.py file in the project root.

subrule.description: Do not create or manage virtual environments (venv, .env, etc.) in code or project scaffolding; environment creation and activation are assumed to be handled externally by the user or tooling.

Do not create any separate files to run the app (such as run.py, manage.py, shell scripts, or batch files); the only entry point for the application should be an app.py file located at the root of the project.
Ensure all setup and startup logic needed to run the application is contained within app.py (plus any imported modules), so running the app is as simple as invoking the Python interpreter on app.py.

rule.description: Error Logging: All unhandled errors and exceptions occurring in the application must be logged to an errors.log file at the project root.

subrule.description: Configure a centralized logging setup (e.g., Python's logging module) that writes error-level logs and above to a file named errors.log in the project root.

Register global exception handlers or middleware in FastAPI so that any unhandled exceptions are captured, logged (including timestamp, path, and traceback where possible), and then converted into a standardized error response.
Do not scatter ad-hoc file writes to errors.log throughout the codebase; all error logging must go through the centralized logger configuration.

rule.description: Comment Blocks Before Routes and Functions: Every route (e.g., FastAPI path operation) and every function definition must have a multi-line ASCII box comment block immediately above it, following the formatting defined in rule 13.
README Creation: Do not create any README files of any kind (e.g., README, README.md, README.txt) anywhere in the project, and do not suggest generating them in scaffolding or documentation.
